Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 15359 of 2023
Applicant :- Sarvesh Kumar

Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Ashok Kumar Singh
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.

Heard Sri Ashok Kumar Singh, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Amit Kumar Shukla,
learned brief holder for the State-respondent.

2. The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.
275 of 2022, under Sections 376, 354-C, 452 IPC Section 66-E and 67-A of the Information Technology Act, 2000, Police Station- Bindaki, District- Fatehpur, during pendency of the trial in the court below.
3.

FIR of the present case was lodged on 26.6.2022 under Sections 452, 354-A, 504, 506 IPC and according to the FIR, on 15.11.2021 at about 11:00 a.m. in the morning when informant was alone at her home, applicant tried to out-rage her modesty and co-accused Seepu prepared the videograph of the incident and pressurized her for his favour and in the FIR it is further mentioned that due to fear earlier informant could not lodge the FIR and when her husband, who resided in Gujarat, returned then she had came to police station along with him.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that entire allegations made against the applicant are totally false and baseless and applicant is a distant relative of the informant and due to some dispute Sarvesh Kumar vs State Of U.P. on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55901035/

sentences.text: 1 in relation, applicant was implicated in the present matter along with Seepu.

5. He further submitted that initially FIR of the present case was lodged under Section 452, 354,
504, 506 IPC and there was no allegation of rape but when the statement of the victim was recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. then she stated that applicant committed rape with her.

He further submitted that victim also made allegation of rape against the applicant in her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C but her both the statements could not be believed as earlier in the FIR,
which was lodged by the victim herself, there was no allegation of rape.

6. He further submitted that incident is although, said to have been take place in the month of November, 2021 but FIR of the present case was lodged on 26.6.2022 after about seven months and this fact itself shows that FIR is based on wrong and false facts.
He further submitted that applicant is not having any criminal history and in the present matter, he is in jail since 15.1.2023.

7. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that in both the statements of the victim, there is specific allegation against the applicant that applicant committed rape with her and in her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. she stated that applicant has also taken indecent photographs of the her and thereafter co-accused Seepu viraled the same but could not dispute the fact that FIR of the present case was lodged after about seven months and in spite of the fact that FIR was lodged by victim herself in the FIR, she did not make any allegation of rape against the applicant.
8.
I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

9. Although, there is allegation of rape against the applicant in both the statements of the victim recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. and 164 Cr.P.C. but victim is a grown up married lady and she admitted that applicant is her relative and her husband resided in Gujarat.

10. Further, the incident of alleged rape and out-raging the modesty of the victim is said to have been taken place in the month of November, 2021 but in spite of that FIR of the present case was lodged on 26.6.2022 i.e. after seven months although, victim tried to explain the delay by stating that due to fear she earlier could not lodge the FIR as her husband was in Gujarat.
Be that as it may

,
fact
remains FIR of the present case was lodged after about seven months.

11. Further in the FIR, which was lodged by the victim herself, there was no allegation of rape but when the statement of the victim was recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. then she first time stated that applicant committed rape and same story was repeated by her in her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C.

, therefore, it appears that there is major deviation in story narrated by her in FIR and in both her statements recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. and 164 Cr.P.C.
12.
Therefore, from the discussion made above, in my view applicant is entitled to be released on bail.

14. Let the applicant- Sarvesh Kumar be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
15. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.
